newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LEND LEASE YEAR PROFIT SEEN UP OVER 10 PCT.
newsitem.headline: LEND LEASE YEAR PROFIT SEEN UP OVER 10 PCT.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd is expected to report on Thursday a rise of over 10 percent in pre-abnormal profit for the year.

Analysts said forecast Lend Lease to report a pre-abnormal net profit of between A$306.0 million and A$330.0 million for the year to June 30 with a median consensus of A$317.7 million, a rise of 13 percent on the 1996/97 figure of A$280.0 million.
The company's two main operations, financial services and property, are expected to contribute increased profits in the 1996/97 year, analysts said.

Lend Lease shareholders are expected to be treated with a rise in final dividend payment to 50 cents a share, compared with 47 cents a year ago, making a total dividend payment of 98 cents for 1996/97 compared with 90 cents in 1995/96.
One Melbourne-based analyst forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$315 million for 1996/97. "I think you will find a bit more on the property side this year," he said.
The analyst said the profit would also be enhanced by the dividend stream from Westpac Banking Corp warrants.
Last year, Lend Lease cut its Westpac stake to about three percent from about nine percent through a warrant issue to institutions.
Analysts said the dividend contribution from Lend Lease's informational technology joint venture with International Business Machines Corp was likely to range between A$6.0 million and A$10 million.
The IBM Global Network venture, formally called ISSC Australia, was expanded last month when Telstra Corp finalised an agreement to join the venture.
Another Melbourne-based analyst forecast Lend Lease to report an annual pre-abnormal net profit of A$321 million.
Lend Lease plans to break down the results from its insurance and funds management arms. Previously these segments were reported under the one heading, financial services.
"I think it will be a moderately tough year (for financial services)," said the second analyst.
Analysts expect a further rise in profit the current year with a consensus forecast of about A$355 million or about an 11 percent rise on the 1996/97 average forecast.

"They never want to suprise people," said the first analyst, who is tipping a pre-abnormal net profit of A$350 million for 1997/98. "You can do all the analysis you like, but they just smooth out the profit year to year," he said.

Lend Lease has been one of the strongest performers on the Australian Stock Exchange since the beginning of the 1996/97 year. To the end of last week, its share price had risen about 58 percent since July 1, 1996.
